children.name: Apus
children.description: Masters of aerial life — swifts sleep, eat, drink, and even mate on the wing, landing only to nest. Common swifts arrive in Swedish towns in May and leave in July, spending the rest of the year airborne over Africa. Their screaming parties around rooftops on summer evenings are one of the defining sounds of Swedish cities.

children.name: Apus apus
children.description: The common swift is a medium-sized bird, superficially similar to the barn swallow or house martin but somewhat larger, though not stemming from those passerine species, being in the order Apodiformes. The resemblances between the groups are due to convergent evolution, reflecting similar contextual development. The swifts' nearest relatives are the New World hummingbirds and the Southeast Asian treeswifts.

children.name: Apus nipalensis
children.description: The house swift (Apus nipalensis) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Apus affinis
children.description: The little swift (Apus affinis) is a small species of swift found in Africa and southwestern Asia, and are vagrants and local breeders in southern Europe.

children.name: Apus caffer
children.description: The white-rumped swift (Apus caffer) is a species of swift. Although this small bird is superficially similar to a house martin, it is not closely related to that passerine species. The resemblances between the swallows and swifts are due to convergent evolution reflecting similar life styles.

children.name: Apus horus
children.description: The Horus swift (Apus horus) is a small bird in the swift family Apodidae that is found in sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Apus barbatus
children.description: The African black swift (Apus barbatus), also known as the African swift or black swift, is a medium-sized bird in the swift family. It breeds in Africa discontinuously from Liberia, Cameroon, Zaire, Uganda and Kenya southwards to South Africa. The "black swifts" of Madagascar and the Comoros are either taken as two subspecies of the African black swift, or otherwise deemed a full species, the Malagasy black swift.

children.name: Apus unicolor
children.description: The plain swift (Apus unicolor) is a medium-sized swift.

children.name: Apus acuticauda
children.description: The dark-rumped swift (Apus acuticauda) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It is found in Bhutan and Northeast India and is a vagrant to Thailand. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Apus pacificus
children.description: The Pacific swift (Apus pacificus) is a species of bird that is part of the Swift family.

children.name: Apus berliozi
children.description: Forbes-Watson's swift (Apus berliozi) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It breeds in coastal areas of Somalia and the southern Arabian Peninsula and on the island of Socotra. In the non-breeding season it has been observed as far south as coastal Mozambique.

children.name: Apus alexandri
children.description: The Cape Verde swift or Alexander's swift (Apus alexandri) is a small bird of the swift family found only in the Cape Verde Islands. It has been recorded from all the islands except Santa Luzia although it probably breeds only on Santiago, Fogo, Brava, Santo Antão and São Nicolau. It is generally common with a stable population and is not considered to be threatened. The name Alexander's swift commemorates Boyd Alexander, an English ornithologist who led two expeditions to the islands in 1897.

children.name: Apus balstoni
children.description: The Malagasy black swift (Apus balstoni) or Madagascar swift, is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It is endemic to Madagascar and the Comoro Islands.

children.name: Apus batesi
children.description: Bates's swift (Apus batesi) is a species of small swift in the family Apodidae which is found in western Africa.

children.name: Apus bradfieldi
children.description:
Bradfield's swift (Apus bradfieldi) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.
It is found in Angola, Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa.

children.name: Apus classicus
children.description: A swift of eastern and southern Africa, sometimes treated as a subspecies of the Common Swift but now recognised as distinct by its more southerly breeding range and slightly different calls. Forages over a wide variety of habitats.

children.name: Apus excelsus
children.description: A medium-sized swift of east African highlands with a white rump and deeply forked tail, often forming mixed flocks with other swift species above montane forests.

children.name: Apus niansae
children.description: The Nyanza swift (Apus niansae) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Apus sladeniae
children.description: The African black swift (Apus barbatus), also known as the African swift or black swift, is a medium-sized bird in the swift family. It breeds in Africa discontinuously from Liberia, Cameroon, Zaire, Uganda and Kenya southwards to South Africa. The "black swifts" of Madagascar and the Comoros are either taken as two subspecies of the African black swift, or otherwise deemed a full species, the Malagasy black swift.

children.name: Apus toulsoni
children.description: The Loanda swift (Apus horus toulsoni) is a bird in the family Apodidae. Many taxonomists consider it to be a subspecies of the Horus swift. It is found in Angola and Republic of the Congo.

children.name: Tachymarptis
children.description: Large, powerful swifts with white bellies.

children.name: Tachymarptis melba
children.description: The alpine swift (Tachymarptis melba) is a species of swift found in Africa, southern Europe, and Asia.

children.name: Tachymarptis aequatorialis
children.description: The mottled swift (Tachymarptis aequatorialis) is a species of bird in the swift family, Apodidae.

children.name: Chaetura
children.description: Spinetailed swifts of the Americas with stiff, spine-tipped tail feathers used to brace against vertical surfaces; many nest in hollow trees and chimneys.

children.name: Chaetura pelagica
children.description: The chimney swift (Chaetura pelagica) is a bird belonging to the swift family Apodidae.

children.name: Chaetura vauxi
children.description: Vaux's swift (Chaetura vauxi) is a small swift native to North America, Central America, and northern South America. It was named for the American scientist William Sansom Vaux.

children.name: Chaetura brachyura
children.description: The short-tailed swift (Chaetura brachyura) is a bird in the Apodidae, or swift family.

children.name: Chaetura cinereiventris
children.description: The grey-rumped swift or gray-rumped swift (Chaetura cinereiventris) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found in Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, and Panama; in every mainland South American country except Chile, French Guiana, Suriname, and Uruguay; in Trinidad and Tobago; and on Grenada.

children.name: Chaetura spinicauda
children.description: The band-rumped swift (Chaetura spinicaudus) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found from Panama south through Colombia into Ecuador, east from Venezuela into the Guianas and Brazil, and on Trinidad.

children.name: Chaetura chapmani
children.description: Chapman's swift (Chaetura chapmani) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Peru, Suriname, Trinidad, Venezuela, and possibly Ecuador.

children.name: Chaetura andrei
children.description: The ashy-tailed swift or Andre's swift (Chaetura andrei) is a Vulnerable species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is endemic to northern and central Venezuela.

children.name: Chaetura bourcierii
children.description: A mid-sized spinetail swift of Andean foothills from Colombia to Ecuador with a contrastingly pale rump, foraging over humid forest. Identification tricky where it overlaps with similar Chaetura species.

children.name: Chaetura egregia
children.description: The pale-rumped swift (Chaetura egregia) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

children.name: Chaetura fumosa
children.description: The Costa Rican swift (Chaetura fumosa) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

children.name: Chaetura josephinae
children.description: A large, pale-rumped Chaetura of Guyana and adjacent Amazonian Brazil, one of the larger spinetail swifts, nesting in the hollows of large rainforest trees.

children.name: Chaetura martinica
children.description: The Lesser Antillean swift (Chaetura martinica) is a species a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found on Dominica, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent, and possibly Nevis.

children.name: Chaetura meridionalis
children.description: Sick's swift (Chaetura meridionalis) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It was previously considered conspecific with the smaller ashy-tailed swift, but a study published in 1997 found that Sick's swift was closer to the chimney swift. The English name commemorates the German-born ornithologist Helmut Sick who studied South American birds. It is a migratory species that breeds in central South America and overwinters in northern South America. The IUCN has listed it as being of "Least Concern".

children.name: Chaetura ocypetes
children.description: The short-tailed swift (Chaetura brachyura) is a bird in the Apodidae, or swift family.

children.name: Chaetura richmondi
children.description: A spinetail swift of Central America from Mexico to Panama with a dark, glossy plumage and pale rump, foraging in flocks above forest canopy.

children.name: Chaetura thomensis
children.description: A spinetail swift endemic to the island of São Tomé in the Gulf of Guinea, one of Africa's few Chaetura swifts. It nests in hollow trees of the island's montane rainforest.

children.name: Chaetura viridipennis
children.description: Chapman's swift (Chaetura chapmani) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Peru, Suriname, Trinidad, Venezuela, and possibly Ecuador.

children.name: Cypseloides
children.description: Large, dark swifts of the Americas that nest in caves and behind waterfalls; among the most aerial of birds.

children.name: Cypseloides niger
children.description: The American black swift, or more simply black swift (Cypseloides niger), is a species of bird that is found from northern British Columbia in Canada through the United States and Mexico to Costa Rica and Brazil. They are also found in the Caribbean.

children.name: Cypseloides cryptus
children.description: The white-chinned swift (Cypseloides cryptus) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It is found from Mexico south through most Central America countries into South America as far south as Peru and east as far as Suriname.

children.name: Cypseloides fumigatus
children.description: The sooty swift (Cypseloides fumigatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Cypseloidinae of the swift family Apodidae.

children.name: Cypseloides cherriei
children.description: The spot-fronted swift (Cypseloides cherriei) is a species of bird in subfamily Cypseloidinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

children.name: Cypseloides lemosi
children.description: The white-chested swift (Cypseloides lemosi) is a species of bird in subfamily Cypseloidinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and possibly Brazil.

children.name: Cypseloides phelpsi
children.description: The tepui swift (Streptoprocne phelpsi) is a species of bird in subfamily Cypseloidinae of the swift family Apodidae.

children.name: Cypseloides rothschildi
children.description: Rothschild's swift (Cypseloides rothschildi) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Cypseloidinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found in Argentina and Bolivia.

children.name: Cypseloides senex
children.description: The great dusky swift (Cypseloides senex) is a species of bird in subfamily Cypseloidinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and possibly Bolivia.

children.name: Cypseloides storeri
children.description: The white-fronted swift (Cypseloides storeri) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It is endemic to Mexico. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Streptoprocne
children.description: Large, powerful swifts of the Neotropics, often with white collars, that breed in caves and gorges and forage over huge areas.

children.name: Streptoprocne zonaris
children.description: The white-collared swift (Streptoprocne zonaris) is a species of bird in the subfamily Cypseloidinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found in Mexico, Central America, the Greater and Lesser Antilles, Trinidad, and every mainland South American country.

children.name: Streptoprocne rutila
children.description: The chestnut-collared swift (Streptoprocne rutila) is a species of bird in subfamily Cypseloidinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found from Mexico and Trinidad south to Peru and Bolivia.

children.name: Streptoprocne biscutata
children.description: The biscutate swift (Streptoprocne biscutata) is a species of bird in subfamily Cypseloidinae of the swift family Apodidae.

children.name: Streptoprocne semicollaris
children.description:
The white-naped swift (Streptoprocne semicollaris) is the largest representative of the swift family in the New World and one of the two largest species in the world. Only the purple needletail of Asia may be slightly larger. This bird is found principally in western and central Mexico, with one record on the Guatemalan border.
This species is essentially a bird of wild highland landscapes, where it favors cliff faces, deep river gorges and high crags. Its main habitats are pine-oak forests, tropical deciduous forests and second-growth scrub. This swift is usually found at an elevation of and, much more rarely, down to sea level.

children.name: Aerodramus
children.description: Echolocating swiftlets of the Indo-Pacific that nest in dark caves; the saliva nests of several species are harvested for bird's-nest soup.

children.name: Aerodramus fuciphagus
children.description: The edible-nest swiftlet (Aerodramus fuciphagus), also known as the white-nest swiftlet, is a small bird of the swift family which is found in Southeast Asia. Its opaque and whitish nest is made exclusively of solidified saliva and is the main ingredient of bird's nest soup, a delicacy of Chinese cuisine. Germain's swiftlet (Aerodramus germani) is now treated as conspecific with this species.

children.name: Aerodramus maximus
children.description:
The black-nest swiftlet (Aerodramus maximus) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
Its saliva is one of the main sources of edible nests for bird's nest soup.

children.name: Aerodramus spodiopygius
children.description:
The white-rumped swiftlet (Aerodramus spodiopygius) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.
It is found in American Samoa, Fiji, New Caledonia, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, the Solomon Islands, Tonga, and Vanuatu. Birds in Australia are now treated as a separate species, the Australian swiftlet (Aerodramus terraereginae).

children.name: Aerodramus vanikorensis
children.description: The uniform swiftlet (Aerodramus vanikorensis), also known as the Vanikoro swiftlet or lowland swiftlet, is a gregarious, medium-sized swiftlet with a shallowly forked tail.

children.name: Aerodramus bartschi
children.description: The Mariana swiftlet or Guam swiftlet (Aerodramus bartschi) is a species of swiftlet in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Aerodramus brevirostris
children.description: The Himalayan swiftlet (Aerodramus brevirostris) is a small swift.

children.name: Aerodramus salangana
children.description: The mossy-nest swiftlet (Aerodramus salangana) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. Some taxonomists consider it to be a subspecies of the uniform swiftlet. It is found in northern Borneo, the Natuna and the Derawan Islands and Nias island off western Sumatra. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Aerodramus amelis
children.description: The Ameline swiftlet (Aerodramus amelis), also known as the grey swiftlet is a small bird in the swift family Apodidae.

children.name: Aerodramus ceramensis
children.description: The Moluccan swiftlet (Aerodramus infuscatus) is a small bird in the swift family Apodidae that is found on Sulawesi and on the Maluku Islands in Indonesia.

children.name: Aerodramus elaphrus
children.description: The Seychelles swiftlet (Aerodramus elaphrus) is a small bird of the swift family.

children.name: Aerodramus francicus
children.description: The Mascarene swiftlet or Mauritius swiftlet (Aerodramus francicus) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Aerodramus germani
children.description: The edible-nest swiftlet (Aerodramus fuciphagus), also known as the white-nest swiftlet, is a small bird of the swift family which is found in Southeast Asia. Its opaque and whitish nest is made exclusively of solidified saliva and is the main ingredient of bird's nest soup, a delicacy of Chinese cuisine. Germain's swiftlet (Aerodramus germani) is now treated as conspecific with this species.

children.name: Aerodramus hirundinaceus
children.description: The mountain swiftlet (Aerodramus hirundinaceus) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Aerodramus humphreysi
children.description: An echolocating swiftlet endemic to Chuuk and surrounding Caroline Islands in Micronesia. It nests in limestone sea caves and forages over the forest-covered volcanic interior.

children.name: Aerodramus inquietus
children.description: The Caroline swiftlet (Aerodramus inquietus), also known as the island swiftlet, Micronesian swiftlet, or Caroline Islands swiftlet, is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Aerodramus leucophaeus
children.description: The Tahiti swiftlet or Polynesian swiftlet (Aerodramus leucophaeus) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Aerodramus luzonensis
children.description: A swiftlet confined to Luzon and nearby northern Philippine islands, nesting in sea caves and inland limestone formations. Its nest is a mix of saliva and plant fibres.

children.name: Aerodramus mariae
children.description: A swiftlet recently described from Maratua and nearby Derawan Islands off Borneo, nesting in sea caves along the island coast. Produces a commercially valued saliva nest.

children.name: Aerodramus mearnsi
children.description: The Philippine swiftlet (Aerodramus mearnsi, formerly Collocalia mearnsi) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Aerodramus mentawi
children.description: A cave swiftlet restricted to the Mentawi Islands off the west coast of Sumatra, breeding in sea caves and cliff crevices. Treated as a full species by IOC based on distinct echolocation calls.

children.name: Aerodramus nakamurai
children.description: A swiftlet of the Ryukyu Islands of southern Japan, nesting in sea caves and rock cavities. A relatively recently recognised species, separated from Aerodramus brevirostris by morphology and genetics.

children.name: Aerodramus nuditarsus
children.description: The bare-legged swiftlet (Aerodramus nuditarsus) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It is found in New Guinea, in subtropical and tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Aerodramus orientalis
children.description: Mayr's swiftlet (Aerodramus orientalis) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It is found in New Ireland and Guadalcanal.

children.name: Aerodramus palawanensis
children.description: The Ameline swiftlet (Aerodramus amelis), also known as the grey swiftlet is a small bird in the swift family Apodidae.

children.name: Aerodramus papuensis
children.description: The three-toed swiftlet or Papuan swiftlet (Aerodramus papuensis, formerly Collocalia papuensis) is a species of swift. It is found in New Guinea.

children.name: Aerodramus pelewensis
children.description: The Palau swiftlet (Aerodramus pelewensis) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Aerodramus rogersi
children.description: The Himalayan swiftlet (Aerodramus brevirostris) is a small swift.

children.name: Aerodramus sawtelli
children.description: The Atiu swiftlet or Sawtell's Swiftlet (Aerodramus sawtelli) is a species of bird in the swift family, endemic to Atiu in the Cook Islands.

children.name: Aerodramus terraereginae
children.description: The Australian swiftlet (Aerodramus terraereginae) is a small bird belonging to the genus Aerodramus in the swift family, Apodidae.

children.name: Aerodramus unicolor
children.description: The Indian Swiftlet or Indian Edible-Nest Swiftlet (Aerodramus unicolor) is a small swift.

children.name: Aerodramus vanderbilti
children.description: A swiftlet of the Schouten and Biak Islands off the northern coast of New Guinea, one of several closely related Papuan cave-nesting species. Distinguished by voice and nest characteristics.

children.name: Aerodramus vulcanorum
children.description: The volcano swiftlet (Aerodramus vulcanorum or Collocalia vulcanorum) is a species of bird in the Apodidae family, formerly considered conspecific with the Himalayan swiftlet (Aerodramus brevirostris).The volcano swiftlet is commonly measured at long and characterized as dark gray with an unmissable brown rump band, whereas younger individuals show a less defined band.

children.name: Aerodramus whiteheadi
children.description: Whitehead's swiftlet (Aerodramus whiteheadi) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It is endemic to the Philippines. It is named after the British explorer John Whitehead. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests. Its status is insufficiently known.

children.name: Collocalia
children.description: Small glossy swiftlets of Asia and the Pacific; unlike Aerodramus, most do not echolocate.

children.name: Collocalia esculenta
children.description: The glossy swiftlet (Collocalia esculenta) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Collocalia linchi
children.description: The cave swiftlet or linchi swiftlet (Collocalia linchi) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Collocalia troglodytes
children.description: The pygmy swiftlet (Collocalia troglodytes) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Collocalia affinis
children.description:
The plume-toed swiftlet (Collocalia affinis) is a small bird in the swift family Apodidae. It is found on some eastern Indian Ocean islands, the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, and lowland Borneo.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. It was previously considered a subspecies of the glossy swiftlet.

children.name: Collocalia dodgei
children.description: The Bornean swiftlet (Collocalia dodgei), also referred to as the Kinabalu 'linchi' swiftlet, is a small bird in the swift family Apodidae.

children.name: Collocalia marginata
children.description:
The grey-rumped swiftlet (Collocalia marginata) or grey-rumped swiftlet, is a small bird in the swift family Apodidae. It is endemic to the Philippines where it is found on most islands except Mindanao.
Its natural habitat is tropical moist lowland forests. It was previously considered a subspecies of the glossy swiftlet.

children.name: Hirundapus
children.description: Needletails — the fastest swifts in level flight, powerful large-bodied birds with spine-tipped tails.

children.name: Hirundapus caudacutus
children.description:
The white-throated needletail (Hirundapus caudacutus), also known as the needle-tailed swift or spine-tailed swift, is a large swift in the genus Hirundapus. It is reputed to reach speeds of up to in horizontal flight, but this is unverified because the methods used to measure its speed have not been published. Is more likely, but this is still at least 100 times the bird's length per second.
They build their nests in rock crevices in cliffs or hollow trees. They do not like to sit on the ground and spend most of their time in the air. They feed on small, flying insects like beetles, flies, bees and moths.

children.name: Hirundapus giganteus
children.description:
The brown-backed needletail (Hirundapus giganteus), or brown needletail, is a large swift.
These birds have very short legs which they use only mainly for clinging to vertical surfaces. They never settle voluntarily on the ground and spend most of their lives in the air, living on the insects they catch in their beaks.

children.name: Hirundapus cochinchinensis
children.description: The silver-backed needletail (Hirundapus cochinchinensis) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It is found in Southeast Asia, Sumatra, Java and Taiwan. It is a vagrant to Christmas Island. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Hirundapus celebensis
children.description: The purple needletail (Hirundapus celebensis), or hagibas in Tagalog, is arguably the largest swift in the world .

children.name: Cypsiurus
children.description: Palm swifts — slender, long-tailed swifts that glue their nests to the underside of palm fronds.

children.name: Cypsiurus parvus
children.description: The African palm swift (Cypsiurus parvus) is a small swift.

children.name: Cypsiurus balasiensis
children.description: The Asian palm swift (Cypsiurus balasiensis) is a small swift.

children.name: Tachornis
children.description: Small Neotropical palm swifts associated with palms and feather-pad nests.

children.name: Tachornis squamata
children.description: The fork-tailed palm swift or Neotropical palm swift (Tachornis squamata) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found across most of northern South America and on Trinidad and Tobago.

children.name: Tachornis phoenicobia
children.description: The Antillean palm swift (Tachornis phoenicobia) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found on the Caribbean islands of Cuba, Jamaica, and Hispaniola (shared by the Dominican Republic and Haiti).

children.name: Panyptila
children.description: Swallow-tailed swifts of the Americas that build long, tubular hanging nests of plant down and saliva.

children.name: Panyptila sanctihieronymi
children.description: The great swallow-tailed swift (Panyptila sanctihieronymi) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found in Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

children.name: Panyptila cayennensis
children.description: The lesser swallow-tailed swift or Cayenne swift (Panyptila cayennensis) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae. It is found from southern Mexico through Central America; in every mainland South America country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay; and on Trinidad.

children.name: Telacanthura
children.description: Large African spinetail swifts with white throats and rumps that nest in hollow trees.

children.name: Telacanthura usheri
children.description: An African spinetail swift with a white throat and rump band, nesting in hollow baobabs and other large trees. Spine-tipped tail aids clinging.

children.name: Raphidura
children.description: Small spinetail swifts with silvery-white rumps.

children.name: Raphidura sabini
children.description: A small, glossy black spinetail swift with a brilliant white rump, hawking insects above the canopy of West and Central African rainforest.

children.name: Rhaphidura
children.description: Small Asian spinetail swift with a bright white rump and needle-tipped tail feathers, related to African Raphidura.

children.name: Rhaphidura leucopygialis
children.description: The silver-rumped spinetail or silver-rumped needletail (Rhaphidura leucopygialis, sometimes spelled Raphidura leucopygialis) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, and Thailand. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. Research on the silver- Rumped spine tail has utilized facultative heterothermy, or even torpor, as a physiological mechanism to reduce its metabolic rate and conserve energy in its tropical environment.

children.name: Mearnsia
children.description: Small Australasian spinetail swifts with boldly patterned black-and-white plumage, closely related to Zoonavena.

children.name: Mearnsia novaeguineae
children.description: The Papuan spinetail (Mearnsia novaeguineae), also known as the Papuan needletail, New Guinea spine-tailed swift or Papuan spine-tailed swift, is a species of swift native to the island of New Guinea.

children.name: Mearnsia picina
children.description: The Philippine spinetail (Mearnsia picina), also known as the Philippine needletail or Philippine spine-tailed swift, is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Zoonavena
children.description: Small African and Malagasy spinetail swifts with white rumps, adapted to forest and open woodland.

children.name: Zoonavena grandidieri
children.description: The Madagascar spinetail, Madagascan spinetail or Malagasy spinetail (Zoonavena grandidieri) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Zoonavena marginata
children.description: A spinetail swift of Madagascar with white-edged inner wing feathers, foraging over forest margins and open farmland. Often seen in fast, erratic flocks over highland rice paddies.

children.name: Zoonavena thomensis
children.description: The São Tomé spinetail (Zoonavena thomensis) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It is endemic to São Tomé and Príncipe, occurring in both São Tomé and Príncipe Islands. The species was described by Ernst Hartert on 1900.

children.name: Zoonavena sylvatica
children.description: The white-rumped spinetail or white-rumped needletail (Zoonavena sylvatica) is a species of swift found in the forests of Bangladesh, India (the Western Ghats) and Nepal. It is often seen over waterbodies in the middle of forest. It can resemble a house swift but has a white vent.

children.name: Neafrapus
children.description: Small, bat-like African spinetail swifts with very short, stumpy tails and broad wings, foraging in flickering flight over forest.

children.name: Neafrapus boehmi
children.description:
Böhm's spinetail, also Bohm's spinetail or Boehm's spinetail, (Neafrapus boehmi), also known as the bat-like spinetail, is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.
It is found in Angola, Botswana, DRC, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Somalia, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. It occurs in the vicinity of Baobab trees and nests in cavities in the trees.

children.name: Neafrapus cassini
children.description: Cassin's spinetail (Neafrapus cassini) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. It is found throughout the African tropical rainforest (including Bioko).

children.name: Schoutedenapus
children.description: African spinetail swifts of highland forest, closely related to Chaetura but restricted to the Afrotropics.

children.name: Schoutedenapus myoptilus
children.description: The scarce swift (Schoutedenapus myoptilus) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Schoutedenapus schoutedeni
children.description: The scarce swift (Schoutedenapus myoptilus) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae.

children.name: Hydrochous
children.description: A monotypic genus of waterfall swifts in Southeast Asia, specialised for nesting behind fast-flowing cascades.

children.name: Hydrochous gigas
children.description: The giant swiftlet (Hydrochous gigas), also known as the waterfall swift, is a species of bird in the swift family, Apodidae.
